sources.title: TBM Framework
supports: Four layers: Foundations, TBM Model, TBM Outcomes, Organizational Value Drivers.
The TBM Model lists connected standards, including Agile, Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM), FinOps and IT financial management.
sources.limits: Layer names taken from page text and figure captions; the figure itself was not inspected. Listing 'Benchmark' as a TBM outcome does not mean this app provides benchmarks.
sources.license: All rights reserved. Framework graphics are not reproduced.

sources.title: TBM Taxonomy
supports: Layers: Technology Cost Pool, Technology Resource Towers, Technology Solutions, Technology Consumer.
The Technology Consumer layer was renamed in version 5.0 (previously 'Business Layer').
Finance, IT and Business views are cross-sections, not layers.
notVerified: Sub-categories and white paper content (likely members only).
sources.limits: Only the public taxonomy page was read.
sources.license: No licence note on the page; treated like S-TBM-1.

sources.title: Lean Portfolio Management
sources.version: SAFe 6.0 (inferred indirectly, not stated on the page)
supports: LPM covers strategy and investment funding, Agile portfolio operations and Lean governance.
LPM governs a specific portfolio within an enterprise.
sources.limits: Public part of the article only.
sources.license: Copying text or images requires written permission. SAFe is a registered trademark.

sources.title: Lean Portfolio Management Discipline
supports: Larger enterprises may manage multiple portfolios.
Strategic themes are adapted at portfolio level.
Enabling agility with enterprise architecture is one of the discipline's competencies.
notVerified: Three of nine competencies were not yet published.
sources.limits: Does not describe a governance layer above multiple portfolios; the enterprise portfolio layer in this app is our own synthesis.
sources.license: Copying text or images requires written permission. SAFe is a registered trademark.

sources.title: Lean Budgets
sources.version: SAFe 6.0 (inferred indirectly, not stated on the page)
supports: Lean budgets fund value streams instead of projects.
Each portfolio operates within an approved budget.
notVerified: Guardrails, participatory budgeting and cadence (behind login).
sources.limits: Public part of the article only.
sources.license: Copying text or images requires written permission. SAFe is a registered trademark.

sources.title: CapEx and OpEx
supports: Lean budgets can contain both CapEx and OpEx.
Labour for software development can be capitalised; finance should be involved early.
sources.limits: Accounting rules are country- and company-specific.
sources.license: Copying text or images requires written permission. SAFe is a registered trademark.

sources.title: Epic
supports: Business and enabler epics.
An epic requires an MVP, a Lean business case and a cost estimate, and is governed through the portfolio Kanban.
notVerified: Epic hypothesis statement and business outcome hypothesis (behind login).
sources.limits: Public part of the article only.
sources.license: Copying text or images requires written permission. SAFe is a registered trademark.

sources.title: The IT4IT Standard
supports: Covers the digital product portfolio at scale and product-based investment models.
Covers the lifecycle from investment decision to end of life.
sources.limits: Based on the publication page. The 'About IT4IT' page still describes version 2.1 and is not used.
sources.license: Commercial use requires a licence. Use for training LLMs or generative AI is prohibited.

sources.title: IT4IT certification programme FAQ
supports: Seven value streams: Evaluate, Explore, Integrate, Deploy, Release, Consume, Operate.
sources.limits: Taken from the certification FAQ and syllabus, not from the standard text.
